content:
dmitri_eval: Nightly eval spike: codegen promptset failures jumped ~1% -> ~10% overnight. Parser crashes on outputs with malformed fenced code blocks (unclosed ```). Attaching a representative sample from the failing run.

--- sample output ---
User: Show fibonacci in python
Model output:
```python
def fib(n):
    a, b = 0, 1
    while a < n:
        yield a
    # intended to close here but model emitted extra tokens and never closed fence
# extra trailing text that includes a stray backtick: `

# downstream parser fails with: ValueError: unmatched fence at position 234
--- end sample ---

This is coming from the int8-packedkv v2.3 canary we promoted last night (canary ~5% traffic). fp16 v2.2 baseline not affected.

alice_ml: Which prompt subset? full codegen or specific langs?

dmitri_eval: It's concentrated in the "short-code-snippets" subset and some longer multi-fence examples. Job: nightly-eval/2026-03-19-23, run id 7482. Logs: s3://redwood-evals/nightly/2056789012/7482/logs.tar.gz

carmen_research: Quick look: sample indicates fence tokens produced mid-sequence without closing. Could be tokenizer detokenization boundary issue — the triple-backtick sequence might be split across tokens differently after quantization.

ben_infra: I can pull the canary pods and full generation traces. Which model artifact tag exactly?

dmitri_eval: model=int8-packedkv:v2.3-canary-2026-03-19

alice_ml: Do we have a token-level diff between v2.2 and v2.3 for the same prompts? even small shift in tokenization can break fence alignment.

carmen_research: Working on reproducing locally with the quantized weights + our detokenizer. Hypothesis: positional embedding indexing off-by-one for sequences that include fence markers (token id sequence length edge-case). Will run unit test that programmatically inserts repeated fence tokens.

ben_infra: Started canary rollback on pool c-canary-23 at 2056789150. Notifying deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated by ben_infra for model int8-packedkv:v2.3 -> int8-packedkv:v2.2. Status: in_progress.

dmitri_eval: After rollback runner triggered a re-eval on Canary subset. Early numbers: failure rate dropped to ~1.2% (close to baseline). Full suite still running.

elaine_prodsec: If parser crashes are upstreaming to customer infra, we should add a temporary tolerant parsing fallback (strip unmatched fences) to avoid crashes. Also recommend gating rule: if codegen promptset parser-failures > 3% in canary, block rollout and auto-rollback.

alice_ml: Actionable items (owners):
1) carmen_research: add deterministic unit test covering triple-backtick boundary tokens + run quantization parity checks.
2) eng-runtime (ben_infra): ensure canary auto-rollback when parser failure threshold exceeded; add alert.
3) dmitri_eval: re-run nightly eval with additional log-level token dumps for failing examples and attach to ticket.
4) devex: add a preprocessing sanitization step in post-gen pipeline that strips/normalizes unmatched fences as temporary mitigation.

carmen_research: I'll also re-run quantization with an alternate packing strategy to see if the tokenization alignment changes. If we confirm positional off-by-one, we'll pin v2.3 until fix and add a regression test in the quant pipeline.

ben_infra: Canary rollback completed at 2056789205. deploy-bot: status -> success. Re-running canary checks now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully for int8-packedkv:v2.3 -> v2.2.

dmitri_eval: Final note: keep v2.3 blocked from full rollout. I'll open a ticket with attached failure census, representative traces, and token-level diffs. Will post ticket id here when created.

alice_ml: Thanks. Let's treat this as high priority; codegen promptset is customer-facing.

(ends)
